featured_reviews.name: Sanchit Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in the beautiful NESCO IT park, this Pan-Asian restaurant is a good place to enjoy Asian food (of course) and have a good time with friends.

The ambiance of the place is really well done with the vibe makes you feel seated at some Oriental place while they also have the special menu according to the Asian festivals.. example they had a special Chinese new year's menu when I visited this place! Also, there are couple of seatings, indoor one is air conditioned while the outdoor has a good open space with heights tables if you want to sit.

Service of the place is above average from what I felt. The server though helpful was taking a bit of time to deliver the food at the table.

Coming over to food we had ordered:
1) Foo Bao(Spicy Chicken): This had a hard covering to keep the fillings intact while had shitake mushroom and chicken as the filling. It was served with a side of peanut sauce and it was an interesting combination.

2) Sriracha Chicken Dumpling: Our server had recommended this thing and it actually turned out to be good... Especially thanks to the sauces server on the side which was the key to make it a success! The filling was simple with minced chicken, carrot, onion and red chili while served with Chilli oil, jalapeno sauce, soy sauce and imperial sauce being served. Jalapeno sauce was an interesting concept though!

3) Foo Blue Butter Japanese Fried Rice: This is one of the must try on their menu, they use the blue pea flower to give the color. The rice though felt regular as usual with a slight buttery taste while we had chicken as an add-on.

4) Foo Yellow curry: The yellow curry was just amazing! Simple gravy made out of coconut milk, french beans, brocolli and water chestnut just made it amazing and i thoroughly enjoyed it!

Given the price of the food items, i wish the quantity served was better.

Overall an amazing place to visit and enjoy the food.

Asia Kitchen by Mainland China, Goregaon East — we went after ages. And before you ask, yes, hope was cautiously packed along with appetite.

First pleasant surprise? A proper menu card. A real, hold-it-in-your-hand, flip-the-pages menu. Not a QR code that demands network, patience and reading glasses. In 2026, this felt revolutionary.

We began with the Vietnamese chicken noodle soup — light, comforting, refreshingly gentle. The kind that doesn’t shout, just quietly does its job. Very demure. Very mindful.

Next came the mushroom cheung fun — soft, silky Hong Kong–style rice rolls that almost redeemed the evening. Moist, delicate, flavourful. The kind of dish that makes you pause mid-sentence.

Then the mains arrived. Five-spice grilled lamb chops. Flavour? Lovely. Texture? The lamb appears to have gone to the gym before arriving on my plate. Chewy is polite. It was less “cut with a knife” and more “earn your protein.” Two pieces at ₹600-plus-tax — that’s ₹300 per chop. At that price, I expect tenderness. Not a jawline workout. The poor lamb gave its life. It needn’t have done so in vain!

The asparagus and sun-dried tomato jasmine fried rice was… philosophical. Four heads of asparagus, five minuscule bits of sun-dried tomato and some green apple — though there were more letters in “green apple” than actual pieces of green apple. It was like playing culinary treasure hunt!

Service was okayish, despite only four tables being occupied. They added a discretionary service charge, which they waived off without drama when asked — so points for that.

Overall? Portions have shrunk. Prices have grown. Enthusiasm has… adjusted accordingly.

We went to Asia Kitchen after a long time. We’ll be going again after a long time more.

featured_reviews.name: Nitin Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
This restaurant is a fantastic choice for Chinese cuisine, standing out for both its flavors and service. With a price of ₹2000+ for two, it offers good value for the quality provided. One visit is sure to make you come back for more!

Food:
Having explored various Chinese dishes before, we decided to rely on the server’s recommendations, and they did not disappoint! The food was served piping hot, bursting with flavors. Do note that some items may be discontinued or unavailable at times, depending on the menu updates.

Soups: The Veg Eight Treasure Soup was a great way to kickstart the meal, setting the perfect tone.

Starters: The Crispy Corn Chilly Pepper had a unique crunch and was full of flavor.

Main Course: The Veg Lemon Grass Fried Rice carried a subtle yet delightful lemongrass aroma. The Veg Nasi Goreng had a well-balanced taste, and the Stir-Fried Chicken with Chilly Garlic & Hot Basil was delicious, though the texture was slightly inconsistent.

Curries & Noodles: The Chicken Thai Red Curry had a rich taste, but the boiled chicken didn’t do it justice—battered pieces would be a better alternative. The Lotus Stem & Asparagus in Red Curry Infusion is a must-try if you enjoy bold flavors. The Wok Tossed Noodles were fairly standard Hakka noodles. The Stir-Fried Crabmeat in Thai Yellow Curry was quite spicy but became well-balanced when mixed with a coconut base. The Crispy Chicken Katsu Baos were decent but could be elevated with the addition of flavorful sauces.

Desserts: The Caramel Sponge Cake with Toffee Sauce was soft and delicious, while the Chocolate Rolls with Ice Cream had a rich Nutella filling. The newly introduced Mango Pudding is definitely worth trying. The Chocolate Dome, while an impressive concept, felt a bit too much to finish after a full meal.

✅ Must-Try: Eight Treasure Soup (Veg/Chicken), Lemon Coriander Thick Soup, Crispy Corn Chilly Pepper, Stir-Fried Chicken with Yu Xiang Sauce, Veg Lemon Grass Fried Rice, Chicken Thai Red Curry, Dynamite Tofu, Caramel Sponge Cake, and Mango Pudding.
☑️ Can Try: General Tao's Favourite Chicken, Veg Mee Goreng Noodles, Pan-Fried Noodles, Tom Yam Chicken Soup, Hot Chocolate Rolls, Thai Basil Chilli Chicken, Crispy Chicken Katsu Bao, Chocolate Dome, and Thai Exotica Glass.
❌ Let-down: Eggwhite Fried Rice and the Chinese New Year Special Potato Dish.

Service:
The staff is warm, courteous, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations were spot on, and they serve with a smile, making the overall experience enjoyable.

Ambience:
The interiors feature Chinese script carvings, adding an authentic touch, while the background music enhances the experience. The space is decent but not extraordinary.

A solid choice for Chinese food lovers! Definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I am extremely disappointed and frustrated with my recent order from China Hunt. I specifically ordered “Paneer Lajawab,” which, as described in your own menu, is supposed to come in a special medium spicy tomato gravy. Naturally, I was expecting a dish with a red, tangy sauce that matches the flavor profile of tomato-based gravies.
However, what I received was completely different. The gravy was yellow instead of red, and the taste was nothing like what was promised. Instead of a tangy, spicy tomato flavor, the dish tasted more like “Methi Malai Paneer”—it was sweet and had an odd, slightly bitter aftertaste. This is misleading, unacceptable, and feels like a total disregard for customer expectations.
Is this really the standard you hold yourself to? Do you think it’s okay to serve anything under the name of a popular dish and expect customers to just accept it? If your chef can’t distinguish between a tomato-based gravy and a malai methi curry, it’s a huge problem. I paid good money for something completely different and now I feel cheated.
This is not just a minor mix-up—this is a sign of careless attitude toward your menu, your food, and most importantly, your customers.

Wanted to feast on some Japanese cuisine and few momos. Having Japanese cuisine at pocket friendly prices is no where near , however, while surfing for the restaurants on Zomato I came across this one which was deliverable at my location. Adding to it this outlet also had good customer reviews too. Decided to order couple of dishes to try at first hence placed an order for following items from Dimsum Wu:
1)Whole wheat chicken tandoori momos (Recommended)- Chicken momos having generous chicken filling in it and perfectly spiced was indeed fabulous. The main usp I would state is that the outer part was whole wheat which was simply great. Served along 2 traditional dips which were good too.

It had slight sweet texture , I suppose it was of honey that could have been excluded for better taste. The omelette placed upside was superb too and overall taste was decent.

To sum up, the food was mind boggling and I did not expected it to be that good. The place is indeed the best in the game when it comes to Japanese cuisines and Dimsums in delivery portal.

Also, I would like to mention that the delivered food was in tamper proof packaging which was again a big plus. The food delivered was hot and fresh too.
Would recommend dimsum enthusiasts like me to try out this place as it will be your splendid experience!
